assertions.name: unbonded_ghost_cross_term_vanishes
assertions.source: step (1) of the derivation: two nucleon ghosts on disjoint strands form a split link, tr_M factorizes, so the cross term is tr_M(g)². Zero iff the ghost is traceless. pyhecke._TR_M_FRAC[3] − [4] over 2, in ℚ.

assertions.name: ghost_self_gram_norm_is_negative
assertions.source: ⟨g⟩²_G = -0.3763510566259827007968897 at 60 dps. The binding form B(K) ~ ⟨Σ_i g_i⟩²_G is stated as the negative-norm ghost quadratic form; a non-negative value would refute the premise this derivation is conditioned on.

assertions.name: ghost_self_gram_norm_reproduces_at_60_dps
assertions.unit: relative gap, float64 Gram vs 60-dps Gram
assertions.source: ⟨g⟩²_G by two routes: pyhecke.gram.G (float64) and gram_matrix_mp(60) (mpmath). Tolerance is the float64 round-off scale for a quantity of order 1, which is what the coarser of the two routes can carry.

description: EXPLORATORY: derives the bond-extensive hypothesis (B = self + coordination·b*) from bond translation-invariance, given the Part-10 Gram-quadratic binding form. Unbonded ghost pair = split link ⇒ cross-term 0 (traceless factorization); a bond couples them; identical bonds ⇒ constant per-bond b*. Upgrades #3549's conditional bond-extensive hypothesis to derived (modulo the value b*, the H₆ seminormal build). Mean-field/homogeneous reading. No fit.
